**Voica v0.9.0-rc.1 — a release candidate: working through a corporate proxy, a Network tab, and dialogs that actually reach you.**

This is a **candidate, not a release.** It is published as a pre-release on purpose: Voica's own
update check only looks at the latest full release, so nobody is offered this build automatically.
About shows the full version, `0.9.0-rc.1`, so there is always an answer to "which one are you
running".

### Working through a proxy

Voica now works where the only way out is a corporate proxy and a VPN is not allowed.

The diagnosis turned out not to be the obvious one. Routing was never broken — .NET reads the
Windows proxy settings by itself — **authentication** was: the proxy answers `407`, nobody sends
credentials, and from the outside that looks like "the app cannot do proxies". Voica now
authenticates as the Windows user you signed in with, so a domain proxy is answered over SSO. **No
password is typed into Voica and none is stored by it.**

The setting reaches everything Voica does over the network: recognition, the one-time model
download, and update checks.

### The Network tab

A sixth tab, before About. It holds **Use the system proxy** (on by default) and a line saying which
route requests are actually taking — the system proxy, one set for this run, or straight out.

Turning it off is a real need too: a proxy left misconfigured in Windows blocks the app just as
effectively as a missing one.

If the proxy refuses, the message **names its address**. That is the thing to hand to whoever
administers the proxy; "the internet does not work" is not.

### Installing the model by hand

Some networks will not pass 215 MB. The README now documents carrying the local model in on a USB
stick — the three file names, their sizes and SHA-256. Voica checks those sums itself the first
time it loads a model it did not download, and remembers the answer, so a truncated copy says so
instead of turning into gibberish recognition.

### Fixed

- **A chosen local engine is never served by the cloud.** The refusal now comes at the start of the
  dictation, with a way out, instead of the audio quietly going to Groq while the switch reads
  "offline".
- **Choosing the local engine no longer starts a download by itself** — behind a closed proxy that
  was an instant error nobody asked for.
- **Dialogs from the tray reach you.** Having no main window, they were not granted the foreground:
  they appeared behind the window you were working in and only blinked in the taskbar. Settings and
  History opened from the tray menu had the same problem.
- **Settings opens directly on the tab you asked for** — "About" used to show General for a moment
  and then jump, size and all.
- **Identical warnings no longer stack**, and a long status line no longer stretches or overflows
  the Settings window.
- **A failed background update check is silent and takes the daily slot.** In a closed network it
  fails at every launch, so retrying was a stream of nothing useful.

### What is worth checking in this candidate

- Behind your own proxy: a dictation, an update check, and — if you use it — the model download.
  Each failure should name the proxy's address.
- The Network tab's route line against what you know your network does.
- Turning the switch off on a machine that has no proxy: everything should keep working.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.9.0.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

The assets carry the base version `0.9.0`; the build itself reports `0.9.0-rc.1` in About.
Installing over an existing copy keeps your history, settings and API key.

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
